class_id: two copies of one module drift in BOTH directions
feature: any module that exists as two copies — packages/shared/src/repositories/* against web/lib/repositories/*, and any check or helper duplicated across workspaces
symptom: a module exists twice and each copy accumulates something the other lacks, so neither is the good one. The known-duplicate framing ('one is live, one is dead — delete the dead one') is then WRONG and dangerous: deleting the 'dead' copy silently drops whatever only it carried. The tell is a fix whose issue number appears in one copy and not the other; the generic tell is that the two files differ by more than whitespace at all. Universal shape: a fix lands in whichever copy the author happened to open, so over time each copy is ahead on different lines, and the drift is invisible because nothing compares them. Distinct from the plain duplicate class, where one copy is simply stale, because here a merge or a delete must be preceded by a DIFF and a decision per difference.
first_seen: 2026-09-20 — issue #824 / PR #830. `web/lib/repositories/data-conflicts-repository.ts` (629 lines, zero production importers, 14 test importers) lacked the W-79 same-source guard that `packages/shared/src/repositories/data-conflicts-repository.ts` has, and the shared copy lacked an id tiebreaker the web copy had from #358 (`detectedAt` ties reshuffled which conflicts a `limit` cut off). So the guarded copy was missing a fix and the fixed copy was missing the guard. The deletion was scoped as 'remove a dead unguarded duplicate'; had it run without a diff, #358's fix would have been lost with no trace. The fix was ported instead, proven by a regression that went 4 passed/1 failed to 5 passed/5
fix_prs: #830 deletes the web copy, repoints its 14 test importers at the shared one, and PORTS the #358 tiebreaker into the shared copy rather than dropping it. The general remedy is the diff-before-delete step, not the deletion
detection_check: none yet. A check on this class is mechanical and cheap: for any pair of files with the same basename under two workspace roots, fail when they differ by more than a configured allowance, so a duplicate cannot quietly diverge. Until that exists, the mitigation is procedural and belongs in every de-duplication brief: DIFF THE TWO COPIES FIRST, and for each difference state whether it is ported, dropped deliberately, or the reason it does not apply. A de-duplication brief that says only 'delete the dead copy' is an incomplete brief
